question: Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom. A skeleton in the cupboard

options.text: A popular fact which is not hidden
options.label: A

options.text: A popular fact to be kept secret
options.label: B

options.text: An embarrassing fact not to be kept secret
options.label: C

options.text: An embarrassing fact to be kept secret
options.label: D

explanation: "A skeleton in the cupboard" (or closet) refers to a dark, embarrassing, or shameful secret that a person or family tries to keep hidden from the public.

question: Identify the type of clause: `I know that she is coming to the party.`
explanation: Use the "It" replacement test. Replace the clause with "it": "I know [it]". The sentence makes perfect sense. Because the clause acts as the object of the verb "know," it is a Noun Clause.

question: I go to Srinagar by ............... Vande Bharat Express.
explanation: Names of specific, famous modes of transport (trains, ships, airplanes) such as the Vande Bharat Express or the Titanic always take the definite article "The".

question: Choose the correct meaning of the phrase `Kick the bucket`
explanation: "Kick the bucket" is a well-known English idiom that means to die or pass away.

question: Fill in the blanks with the correct tense form of the verb: I am feeling quite full. I ______.
explanation: The action is complete, but the effect is still "alive" in the present ("I am feeling full"). Furthermore, the keyword "just" demands the Present Perfect tense (Have + V3).

question: Choose the correct narration: `How is your father?`, asked my friend.

options.text: My friend asked how was my father?
options.label: A

options.text: My friend asked how is my father?
options.label: B

options.text: My friend asked how my father is.
options.label: C

options.text: My friend asked how my father was.
options.label: D

explanation:
For Wh- Questions in Narration:
1. The Wh- word ("how") acts as the connector.
2. The question format flips to a statement format: "is your father" becomes "my father was" (tense backshifts from present to past).

question:
Find correct sequence of sentence fragments:
P. i have not come to complain he said
Q. even if it means some humiliation
R. but the boy must learn to be honest
S. and admit he broke it.
explanation: P is the natural opener (Main subject/verb). R provides the contrast to his statement ("but the boy must learn"). S continues the boy's action ("and admit"). Q provides the concluding condition ("even if"). Sequence: P - R - S - Q.

question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence: The villagers were enjoying the winter evening around the fire.

options.text: The villagers were enjoying the winter evening around the fire.
options.label: A

options.text: The villagers were enjoying winter evening round a fire.
options.label: B

options.text: The villagers were enjoying a winter evening around fire.
options.label: C

options.text: The villagers was enjoying the winter evening round the fire.
options.label: D

explanation: Specific events or items take the definite article. It is a specific "winter evening" and they are sitting around a specific "fire," so both require "the." Option D incorrectly uses the singular verb "was" for a plural subject.

question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence: The receptionist must answer courteously the questions what are asked by the callers.

options.text: The receptionist must answer courteously the questions what are asked by the callers.
options.label: A

options.text: The receptionist must answer courteously for the questions of all the callers.
options.label: B

options.text: The receptionist should answer courteously the questions of all the callers.
options.label: C

options.text: The receptionist courteously should answer the question of callers.
options.label: D

explanation:
Option C is the most concise and structurally sound.
Option A incorrectly uses "what" instead of "that/which."
Option B uses an incorrect preposition ("answer for").
Option D incorrectly places the adverb "courteously" before the modal.

question: When carefully examined (a)/ it was found that there (b)/ were some missing pieces (c)/ in the evidence given by him (d). Which part has grammatical errors?

options.text: in the evidence given by him
options.label: D

explanation: This is a "Dangling Modifier" error. The phrase "When carefully examined" implies that the subject immediately following the comma is the thing being examined. "It" cannot be examined. The sentence should ideally be restructured, meaning the error lies in Part A.

question: I got up and went out to the veranda for _____ air, but the wind god seemed to have taken time off.
explanation: "Air" is an uncountable noun. "Little" means almost none (negative). "A little" means some amount (positive). The speaker went out for some air, making "a little" the correct choice.

question: On the bedside she discovered a great_____ sheet of fine paper.
explanation: "A great many" is a fixed idiomatic quantifier used to mean 'a very large number of'.

question: Spot the errors, if any, in the following sentence: The three storey building comprises of six houses, two parking lots and one basement.

options.text: The three storey building comprises of six houses
options.label: A

explanation:
The verb "comprise" in active voice NEVER takes the preposition "of". (Consists of = Comprises).
Correction: "The building comprises six houses."

question: Identify the part of speech the bold word in the below sentence belongs to: Jeff longed for a pity party after he lost his job.
explanation: "Longed" is the past tense form of the action verb "long" (meaning to desire or yearn for something).

question: Spot the errors, if any, in the following sentences: Innovations into the field of artificial intelligence can help to increase the wages of the workforce provided workers have the necessary skills.

options.text: artificial intelligence can help to increase
options.label: B

options.text: provided workers have the necessary skills
options.label: D

explanation:
The preposition "into" indicates motion or entry (e.g., jump into the pool). For static concepts or academic fields, the correct preposition is "in".
Correction: "Innovations in the field of..."

question: Spot the errors, if any, in the following sentence: I do not understand why in spite of my best efforts to please him, my boss is so angry at me.

options.text: in spite of my best efforts
options.label: B

options.text: my boss is so angry at me.
options.label: D

explanation:
Fixed Preposition Rule: You are angry with a person, and angry at an action/behavior.
Correction: "...my boss is so angry with me."

question: Fill in the blanks with appropriate prepositions: The officials have the habit of fawning ______ ministers.
explanation: "Fawn upon" (or "fawn on") is a fixed phrasal verb meaning to flatter someone excessively in a servile way.

question: The antonym of the word SYCOPHANTS is:
explanation: A "sycophant" is a self-serving flatterer or parasite (Options A, B, and C are synonyms). "Devoted" implies genuine, selfless loyalty, making it the antonym.

question: Select the synonyms of the word occurring in the sentence in capital letters. Some parties see him as a MUNIFICENT benefactor, while others regard him as an agent of sloth.
explanation: "Munificent" means extremely generous or lavish. "Bountiful" is the closest synonym. (Note: Penurious means extremely poor or stingy, acting as the antonym).

question: The synonyms of the word CIRCUMLOCUTION is:
explanation: "Circumlocution" means using many words to express something vaguely or indirectly. Compression, Succinctness, and Conciseness are all direct antonyms. Euphemism (a mild, indirect expression) is the closest related synonym here.

question: In this question, the sentence is broken into four parts. Find out the error part in the sentence from the given options. The criminal was sentenced to death and was hung for his crime.
explanation:
"Hung" is the past tense used for objects (e.g., hung a picture). "Hanged" is the specific V3 form used exclusively for executing humans by hanging. So Picture is hung and Person is hanged.
Correction: "...and was hanged for his crime."

question: Fill in the blanks with suitable articles: She is wearing a black and ____ white saree at the party hosted by the Manager and ____ Executive Director of our hotel.
explanation:
1. First Blank: It is one single saree containing two colors. Do not repeat the article. (No article).
2. Second Blank: The Manager and the Executive Director refer to two distinct people holding two different posts. The article "The" must be repeated to show they are two separate individuals.

question: Arrange letters AVSEBORINTO into a meaningful word. what will be the position of T from left?
explanation:
The jumbled letters form the word OBSERVATION.
Counting from the left: O(1) B(2) S(3) E(4) R(5) V(6) A(7) T(8). The letter T is at the 8th position.

question:
Which of the options given below the sentence should replace the part underlined to make the sentence grammatically correct?
"Have you been" more careful, the accident could have been averted.
explanation:
This sentence tests the Type 3 Conditional Inversion.
The normal structure for an impossible past condition is: If I had seen him, I would have stopped.
When we remove "If" (Inversion), the auxiliary verb "Had" jumps before the subject: Had I seen him, I would have stopped.
Here, the result clause is "could have been averted" (Modal + Have + V3), meaning the condition must be Past Perfect (Had + V3).

question: The kitchen is ________ the back of the house.
explanation:
When referring to a specific point or exact location in or around a building, we use the preposition "at".
Examples: at the front, at the back, at the door, at the top.

question: He gave a talk ____ the causes of dengue fever.
explanation: The preposition "on" is used to indicate the subject matter or topic of a formal presentation, lecture, book, or talk. It means "about" but is used in more formal/academic contexts.

question:
Choose the correct antonym of the given word:
Dissolute
explanation:
Dissolute means lax in morals, licentious, or indulging in sensual pleasures (a negative word).
Moral means is direct opposite.
Repulsive means disgusting, and Distant means far away.

question:
Choose the correct synonym of the given word:
Consummation
explanation:
Consummation means the point at which something is complete, finalized, or perfected. (e.g., "The consummation of a dream").
Therefore, "Ultimate completion" is the exact synonym.

question: They left early.
explanation:
A clause with a subject ("They") and a verb ("left") that can stand alone as a complete thought is an independent clause.
Since this sentence simply makes a statement or declares a fact, it is specifically a Declarative clause.
Noun, Adjective, and Adverb clauses are dependent (subordinate) clauses, which this sentence is not.

question:
Fill in the blank with correct homophone:
The _____ thread was thrown away.
explanation:
This is a homophone question (words that sound similar but mean different things).
Knotty means full of knots, tangled, or difficult to solve (perfectly fits "thread").
Naughty means badly behaved. Notty and notey are not standard English words.

question:
Fill in the blank with correct homophone:
We sat under the shade of the _____
explanation:
Beech is a type of large tree with smooth grey bark and glossy leaves.
Beach refers to the sandy shore by the ocean.
Breach means a violation of a rule or a gap in a wall.

question:
Choose the correct pronoun:
Let you and ____ try what we can do.
explanation:
Apply The "Let" Rule: Any pronoun that immediately follows the verb "Let" or any preposition (between, except, but) MUST be in the Object Case (me, him, her, us, them).
Wrong: Let you and I try.
Right: Let you and me try.

question:
Pick the right meanings of the following idioms/phrase,
At the drop of the hat:

options.text: As soon as it was spoken
options.label: A

explanation: The idiom "at the drop of a hat" means doing something immediately, instantly, or without any hesitation.

question: I saw ___good deal of him during ___war.
explanation:
1. First Blank: The phrase "a good deal of" is a fixed idiomatic quantifier meaning "a large amount of". It always takes the indefinite article 'a'.
2. Second Blank: We are referring to a specific, known historical event (the war they both experienced). Therefore, it takes the definite article "the".

question: _______ I call the witness?
explanation:
In a formal, legal, or official setting (like a courtroom calling a witness), the most appropriate modal for requesting permission is May.
"Can" is too informal (friendly ability), and "Could" is hesitant. "May" represents the highest degree of formal respect.

question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.text: He had visiting the temple frequently.
options.label: C

options.text: He have had visited the temple frequently.
options.label: D

explanation:
The keyword "frequently" indicates a habitual or repeated action, which demands the Simple Present Tense.
Because the subject "He" is singular, the verb must also be singular (by adding 's' or 'es').
Singular Subject (He) + Singular Verb (visits) = Grammatically correct.

question: Which tense is used to express an action that began in the past before some point and continued up to that point?
explanation:
The Past Perfect Continuous Tense (Had + been + V1+ing) describes an action that started in the past and continued up until another specific point in the past.
Example: I had been studying for two hours before my friend arrived.

question: The thief will have run away before the police ............
explanation:
This tests the Future Timeline Combo (Before/When).
Main Clause (First Action): Future Perfect (will have run away).
Time Clause (Second Action): Must be Simple Present.
Since "police" is treated as a collective noun here acting as a singular unit arriving (or colloquially plural requiring 'come'), the closest Simple Present option provided by the examiner is "comes". (Note: 'police come' is strictly more accurate, but 'comes' is the only present tense option available to satisfy the rule against 'had come' or 'came').

question: What are homonyms?

options.text: Words that sound the same but have different meanings
options.label: A

options.text: Words that are spelled the same but have different meanings
options.label: C

explanation:
Homonyms is an umbrella term that includes:
1. Homophones: Words that sound the same but have different meanings/spellings (e.g., See / Sea) - Option A.
2. Homographs: Words that are spelled the same but have different meanings/pronunciations (e.g., Tear (crying) / Tear (rip)) - Option C.

question: Do not put off till tomorrow what you _____ do today.
explanation:
This is a famous English proverb: "Do not put off till tomorrow what you can do today."
Grammatically, can is used here to show present ability or capacity. If you have the ability to finish something now, do it immediately rather than waiting.

question:
Pick out the relative clause in the following sentence:
If there was scarcity of milk, its prices went up.

options.text: If there was scarcity of milk
options.label: D

explanation:
Note: Though the examiner asked for a "relative clause", this is technically an Adverb Clause of Condition.
In clause identification questions, you must find the dependent (subordinate) clause that cannot stand alone.
"If there was scarcity of milk" begins with the subordinating conjunction "If" and depends entirely on the main clause ("its prices went up") to make sense.

question:
Choose the correct option.
He_______completed his book yesterday.
explanation:
This tests the Dead Time rule. The word "yesterday" is a specific past time indicator. Whenever a sentence mentions a specific point in the past (yesterday, last night, in 1947), you MUST use the Simple Past Tense (V2).
The sentence is already correctly using the V2 form "completed". Using "has completed" or "had completed" would be a grammatical violation.

question:
Fill in the blank using suitable articles. When no article is required, select no article among the given options.
I went to____ hometown last year and remained there for ____ week.
explanation:
1. First Blank: The noun "hometown" refers to a specific, particular place (the speaker's hometown). Therefore, it requires the definite article "the".
2. Second Blank: The phrase "for a week" is a standard idiomatic expression used to indicate the duration of a single numerical unit (one week).

question: What is the masculine form of "goose"?
explanation:
"Goose" is a feminine noun referring to the female bird. Its masculine counterpart is Gander.
FeminineMasculine
GooseGander
DuckDrake
BeeDrone
Sheep (Ewe)Ram

question: Which of the following is a verb?
explanation:
A verb is a word that describes an action, state, or occurrence.
Laughing is the present participle form of the action verb "to laugh".
Joy and Happiness are abstract nouns. Table is a concrete noun.

question: In the sentence "She sings beautifully," the word "beautifully" is a
explanation: An Adverb is a word that modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. In this sentence, "beautifully" modifies the verb "sings" by answering the question: How does she sing?

question: In the sentence "The cat is sleeping on the mat," the word "sleeping" is a
explanation: In this sentence, "sleeping" is the main verb (the present participle form of "sleep"). It works together with the auxiliary (helping) verb "is" to form the present continuous tense, describing the action the cat is performing.

question: What part of speech is the word "quickly" in the sentence: "She runs quickly"?
explanation: The word "quickly" modifies the verb "runs" by describing the manner in which the action is performed. Most words ending in "-ly" that describe actions are adverbs of manner.

question: Which of the following is an example of a common noun?
explanation:
Common Noun: Names a general, non-specific person, place, or thing (e.g., school, planet, boy, monument). They are not capitalized.
Proper Noun: Names a specific, unique entity and is always capitalized (e.g., Taj Mahal, Rahul, Mercury).

question: Choose the sentence that has the correct capital letter usage.

options.text: He went to the cricket match and I went to the music concert.
options.label: A

options.text: He went to the cricket match and i went to the music concert.
options.label: B

options.text: he went to the cricket match and I went to the music concert.
options.label: C

options.text: He went to the cricket match and I went to the music Concert.
options.label: D

explanation:
Core Capitalization Rules:
1. Sentence Openings: The first letter of any sentence must be capitalized ("He").
2. The Pronoun "I": The personal pronoun "I" is ALWAYS capitalized, regardless of where it appears in the sentence.
3. Common Nouns: General words like "cricket match" and "music concert" remain in lowercase unless they are part of a specific proper title.

question:
Pick out the correct meaning of the given idiom/Phrase:
To play ducks and drakes

options.text: To manage resources carefully and effectively
options.label: A

options.text: To be very honest with someone
options.label: C

explanation: The idiom "to play ducks and drakes" means to act recklessly or to squander/waste one's wealth.

question:
Pick out the correct meaning of the given idiom/Phrase:
To brow beat

options.text: To encourage someone with positive reinforcement
options.label: C

explanation: The idiom "to browbeat" means to intimidate or bully someone into doing something, often through stern, arrogant, or fierce looks and words.

question:
Select the antonym of the word:
Languid
explanation:
Languid means slow, relaxed, or lacking in energy/vitality.
Virile means having strength, energy, and a strong sex drive (usually referring to men); energetic and robust.
Languorous, Torpid, and Lackadaisical are all synonyms of Languid.

question:
Read the sentences and underline the subordinate clause.
Although I was not up for a movie, I watched 'Avatar in hall No.5' with my friend.

options.text: Although I was not up for a movie
options.label: C

explanation:
A sentence is divided into main (independent) and subordinate (dependent) clauses. A subordinate clause cannot stand alone to make complete sense and is introduced by a subordinating conjunction (e.g., Although, Because, Since, If, When).
Clause typeExample in sentence
Main ClauseI watched 'Avatar in hall No.5' (Can stand alone)
Subordinate ClauseAlthough I was not up for a movie (Depends on the main clause)
Phrasewith my friend (No subject-verb combo)

question:
Select the most appropriate INDIRECT form of the given sentence
Newton said to Thomas, "how is your research going?"

options.text: Newton asked Thomas how was your research going.
options.label: A

options.text: Newton asked Thomas how his research was going.
options.label: B

options.text: Newton asked Thomas how is your research going.
options.label: C

options.text: Newton wanted to know how was Thomas's research going.
options.label: D

explanation:
Apply the core rules of Narration for 'Wh-' questions:
1. Reporting Verb: "said to" changes to "asked".
2. Conjunction: The 'Wh-' word ("how") acts as the connector. Do not add 'that'.
3. Structure Flip: The question structure (Verb + Subject) must become a statement structure (Subject + Verb).
4. Tense Backshift: Present Continuous ("is going") becomes Past Continuous ("was going").
5. Pronoun Shift: "Your" (2nd Person) changes according to the Object (Thomas) to "his".
Result: Newton asked Thomas how his research was going.

question: This is impossible, it_______be a mistake.
explanation:
When the speaker is making a strong logical deduction based on clear evidence (e.g., "This is impossible"), the correct modal to use for high certainty (99%) is must.
ModalLevel of certaintyUsage
Must99% (Almost Sure)Logical deduction based on evidence.
May/Might50% / 15%Weak or remote possibilities.
CanGeneral TruthTheoretical possibility.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no Improvement is needed, select "NO IMPROVEMENT."
On hearing the news over the radio that India won the football match, I jumped with joy.
explanation:
This question tests the Grandfather Rule (Past Perfect). When two actions happen in the past, the older action must be in the Past Perfect Tense, and the newer action in the Simple Past.
1. Older Action (Grandfather): India won the match (Happened first) -> had won.
2. Newer Action (Father): Hearing the news / Jumped with joy (Happened second) -> heard / jumped (Simple Past).
Therefore, "won" must be improved to "had won".

question: Karan speaks______Spanish. He believes, honesty is _____ best policy.
explanation:
1. First Blank: Languages (Spanish, English, Hindi) do not take an article unless referring to the people of that country e.g., "The Spanish speak spanish".
2. Second Blank: "Best" is a superlative adjective (good -> better -> best). Superlative degrees of adjectives always take the definite article "the".

question:
Given below are four scattered segments of two sentences. Indicate the correct sequence that correctly assembles the segments and completes the sentence.
P. due to rapid urbanization
Q. environmental degradation has increased
R. and unplanned industrial growth
S. in many developing regions
explanation:
"Opener" Hunt: The sentence must start with an independent subject. Segment Q introduces the main topic: "environmental degradation has increased."
Cause-Effect Link: What caused it? "due to rapid urbanization" (P).
Parallel Link: The conjunction "and" connects two similar ideas: "rapid urbanization" and "unplanned industrial growth" (R).
Location: Where is this happening? "in many developing regions" (S).
Sequence: Q - P - R - S.

question:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate homonyms.
The gardener placed a ______ next to the delicate seedling to mark its location for watering.
explanation:
This is a vocabulary question testing homophones (words that sound the same but have different meanings).
Carrot: An orange root vegetable (fits the gardener/seedling context).
Caret: A proofreading mark (^).
Karat: A measure of gold purity (24-karat).
Carat: A unit of weight for gemstones.

question:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate homonyms.
Indian mythology regards the material world as an__________.
explanation:
Illusion: A false perception or deceptive appearance (e.g., a mirage or the concept of 'Maya' in mythology).
Allusion: An indirect reference to something.
Elusion: The act of escaping or avoiding.
Delusion: A false belief held despite strong contradictory evidence (usually clinical or psychological).

question:
In this question, the sentence is broken into four parts. Find out the error part in the sentence from the given options and mark your answer.
The principal (a)/will have started (b)/before I (c)/ could reach there (d).
explanation:
This sentence tests the Future Perfect Timeline Combo.
When an action is expected to be completed in the future before another action takes place:
1. The First Action: Uses Future Perfect (will have + V3) -> "will have started".
2. The Second Action (Time Clause): Clauses starting with "before" or "when" MUST use the Simple Present Tense (V1).
Using past tense modals like "could" is strictly prohibited here.
Correction: Remove "could". The phrase should simply be "before I reach there."

question: Find out the wrongly spelled word.
explanation:
The correct spelling is Etiquette (meaning the customary code of polite behavior). It requires a double 't' at the end.
Acquiesce: To accept something reluctantly but without protest.
Convalesce: To recover health after an illness.
Acquittance: A written receipt showing payment of a debt.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word
UMBRAGE
explanation:
Vocabulary Builder:
Umbrage refers to a feeling of offense, annoyance, or resentment, especially when someone feels slighted or insulted. (Commonly used in the phrase "to take umbrage").
Calmness & Pleasure = Antonyms.
Acclaim* = Praise.

question: Which of the following sentences contains a Possessive Determiner?

options.text: Several of the proposed solutions were rejected due to impracticality.
options.label: A

options.text: Every solution has advantages and disadvantages, but some are more feasible than others.
options.label: B

options.text: Few students understood the complexity of such philosophical arguments.
options.label: C

options.text: They were proud of their achievements in the international competition.
options.label: D

explanation:
Determiner Identification:
A possessive determiner sits before a noun to show ownership (e.g., my, your, his, her, its, our, their).
Option D uses "their achievements", which correctly shows ownership.
Why others are incorrect: "Several" (A) and "Few" (C) are Quantifiers. "Every" (B) is a Distributive determiner.

question: In which sentence is the determiner wrongly used?

options.text: Despite checking each record carefully, the auditor could not detect the financial discrepancy.
options.label: A

options.text: Fortunately, she has some relatives who are always ready to support her in times of need.
options.label: B

options.text: Not much students were aware of the sudden change in schedule.
options.label: C

options.text: Those students participated in the debate competition.
options.label: D

explanation:
Much is used for Uncountable Nouns (Quantity: Much water, Much time).
Many is used for Countable Nouns (Numbers: Many boys, Many students).
"Students" is a plural, countable noun. Therefore, "much students" is a grammatical mismatch. It must be "many students."

question:
Which of the following determiners (Bold) in the sentence are correctly matched with their type?
1- These books are very informative. – Demonstrative determiner
2- She has some doubts about the proposal. – Distributive determiner
3- My brother lives abroad. – Possessive determiner
4- Each student received a certificate. – Quantitative determiner
explanation:
Determiner Classification:
WordTypeLogic
These (1)DemonstrativePoints to specific things (This, That, These, Those).
Some (2)QuantifierShows an undefined amount. (Incorrectly labeled as Distributive).
My (3)PossessiveShows ownership (My, Your, His, Our, Their).
Each (4)DistributiveRefers to members individually. (Incorrectly labeled as Quantitative).
Only pairs 1 and 3 are matched correctly.

question:
Which form of verb is used in the sentence below?
The apparatus functioned as it was originally designed to do, but only after repeated trials.
explanation:
Transitive vs. Intransitive Verbs:
Transitive Verbs demand a direct object. (Ask: What? or Whom?)
Intransitive Verbs do NOT take an object. The action stays with the subject.
In the sentence, the verb "functioned" means operated or worked. It does not transfer action to an object. (You cannot "function" an object). Therefore, it is Intransitive.

question: Which of the following sentences contains an inchoative verb?
explanation:
An Inchoative Verb is a specific type of verb that expresses a change of state, a beginning, or a becoming.
"Darkened" shows the sky transitioning from one state (light) to another state (dark), making it the perfect example of an inchoative verb. Options A, C, and D are standard action verbs.

question: The manager was accused ___ negligence in handling the project.
explanation:
Fixed Prepositions (The Crime/Blame Rule):
The verb accuse (or its passive form "was accused") is strictly followed by the preposition "of".
Exam Trap: Students often confuse this with "punished for" or "charged with".
You are punished FOR a crime.
You are charged WITH a crime.
You are accused OF a crime.

question: She is adept ___ solving complex mathematical problems.
explanation:
Fixed Prepositions (The Skill Rule):
When describing someone's proficiency or skill level at a specific activity, the adjective adept takes the preposition "at".
Memory Trick: Good at, Bad at, Adept at.
Note: The preposition is correctly followed by the gerund form of the verb ("solving").

question:
Change the following sentence from Active voice to Passive voice.
Do the work at once.

options.text: The work should be done at once.
options.label: A

options.text: At once, the work be done by you.
options.label: B

options.text: Let the work be done at once.
options.label: C

options.text: You are asked to do the work at once.
options.label: D

explanation:
Imperative Sentences (Commands WITH an Object):
When an active command has a direct object (like "the work"), the standard passive formula uses Let.
VoiceFormulaExample
ActiveV1 + ObjectDo (V1) the work (Obj)
PassiveLet + Object + BE + V3Let the work be done
Option A is used for moral duty/advice (e.g., Help the poor -> The poor should be helped). Option C is the correct translation for a direct command.

question:
Fill in the blanks with appropriate prepositions.
The management decided to act _____ the recommendation of the expert panel and proceed ___ the proposed reforms.
explanation:
Phrasal Verbs / Fixed Prepositions:
1. Act on: To take action because of a piece of information or advice (e.g., act on a recommendation).
2. Proceed with: To begin or continue a course of action (e.g., proceed with the reforms).

question:
Choose the option that correctly expresses the meaning of the idiom used in the sentence:
The minister 'threw down the gauntlet' by openly questioning the opposition's policy.

options.text: To retreat from a public stance
options.label: A

explanation:
"To throw down the gauntlet" means to issue a direct, open, and bold challenge to someone.
Origin: In medieval times, a knight would literally throw his heavy armored glove (a gauntlet) at the feet of an opponent. If the opponent picked it up, the challenge to a duel was accepted.

question:
Select the sentence that correctly punctuates the given sentence.
I therefore request you to grant me leave.

options.text: I therefore, request you to grant me leave.
options.label: A

options.text: I, therefore, request you to grant me leave.
options.label: B

options.text: I therefore request, you to grant me leave.
options.label: C

explanation:
The "Interrupter" Comma Rule:
When transitional adverbs like therefore, however, or moreover interrupt the natural flow of a sentence (between the subject and the verb), they act as parenthetical elements.
You must place a comma before and after the word to set it off from the rest of the sentence.
Example: I, therefore, request you to grant me leave.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word
WINSOME
explanation:
Vocabulary Builder:
Winsome means charming, attractive, or appealing in a fresh, innocent way.
To find the antonym, we need a word that means unpleasant or driving people away. Repellent perfectly fits this description. Options A, B, and C are synonyms of winsome.

question: Select the correct spelling of the word meaning "A person who talks through his or her hat."
explanation:
The idiom "talking through your hat" means speaking nonsense or talking about something without actually knowing the facts.
A Perlocutionist refers to someone who engages in such speech.

question: Select the correctly spelt word:
explanation:
Sacrilegious (Sac-ri-le-gious) means showing disrespect or violating something sacred.
Exam Trap: Because it relates to religion, students often mistakenly spell it with "religious" (Sacreligious). The correct spelling comes from the Latin root sacrilegium* (sacri + legi + ous).

question: At _____ equator, sunrise occurs at the same time each day.
explanation:
The "Unique & Universal" Rule:
When referring to things that are one of a kind or unique geographical features, always use the definite article The.
Examples: The Sun, The Moon, The Equator, The North Pole.

question: I am going to ____ concert tomorrow.
explanation:
The Indefinite Article Sound Rule:
"Concert" is a singular, countable noun being introduced generally (any concert, not a specific one), so it requires an indefinite article (A/An).
Since "concert" begins with a hard 'C' (consonant sound), it takes "a".

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order.
1- cannot be addressed through isolated actions
2- complex environmental problems
3- that require coordinated global efforts
4- but demand long-term strategic planning
explanation:
The Subject-Modifier-Verb Link:
1. Opener (Subject): Statement 2 introduces the main topic ("complex environmental problems").
2. Modifier: Statement 3 describes those problems ("that require..."). Link: 2 -> 3.
3. Action (Verb): Statement 1 tells us what happens to the subject ("cannot be addressed"). Link: 3 -> 1.
4. Contrast (Conjunction): Statement 4 uses "but" to provide the contrasting solution. Link: 1 -> 4.
Final Sentence: Complex environmental problems (2) that require coordinated global efforts (3) cannot be addressed through isolated actions (1) but demand long-term strategic planning (4).

question: What does the idiom "hit the nail on the head" mean?

options.text: To be exactly right or accurate
options.label: D

explanation: "Hit the nail on the head" means to describe a situation exactly, or to be precisely right about the core cause of a problem.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.text: Neither of the proposals submitted by the committee members were found satisfactory.
options.label: A

options.text: Hardly had the meeting begun when the power cut disrupted the proceedings.
options.label: B

options.text: Each of the participants have expressed their concerns regarding the policy changes.
options.label: C

options.text: The data collected from various sources indicated that the results are inconclusive.
options.label: D

explanation:
The Inversion Rule (Hardly/Scarcely):
When a sentence starts with a negative word like Hardly, the structure must invert to Helping Verb + Subject and it must pair with the conjunction when. (Hardly + had + the meeting + begun + when). Option B is perfectly correct.
Why others are incorrect:
Option A: "Neither" is strictly singular. It must be "was found".
Option C: "Each" is strictly singular. It must be "has expressed".
Option D: Tense mismatch. "Indicated" is past, but "are" is present, so use of "were"

question:
Match the word with its synonym.
1- Ricochet -> a. Carom
2- Melancholy -> b. Heart-rending
3- Poignant -> c. Dejected
4- Subterfuge -> d. Ploy
explanation:
Vocabulary Builder:
WordSynonymMeaning
RicochetCaromTo rebound or bounce off a surface.
MelancholyDejectedA deep feeling of sadness or depression.
PoignantHeart-rendingDeeply moving; evoking a sharp sense of sadness.
SubterfugePloyDeceit or a trick used to achieve a goal.

question:
Given below are four scattered segments of a sentence. Indicate the correct sequence that correctly assembles the segments and completes the sentence.
P- improving the quality of education
Q- requires consistent efforts from
R- teachers, parents, and policymakers
S- in modern society
explanation:
Sentence Arrangement (Subject-Verb-Object Structure):
A standard English sentence follows the S-V-O pattern.
1. Subject (The Core Idea): "Improving the quality of education" (P)
2. Verb (The Action/Requirement): "requires consistent efforts from" (Q)
3. Object (Who must do it): "teachers, parents, and policymakers" (R)
4. Context (Where/When): "in modern society" (S).
Fact Check: The raw input marked a different option, but logically and grammatically, P-Q-R-S is the only coherent sequence.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.text: Neither the teacher nor the students were aware of the sudden change in schedule.
options.label: A

options.text: One of the most important factors influencing the results are temperature variations.
options.label: B

options.text: The number of applicants have increased significantly this year.
options.label: C

options.text: Each of the proposals submitted by the researchers were carefully examined.
options.label: D

explanation:
Subject-Verb Agreement Rules:
RuleApplicationCorrected sentence
Proximity Rule (Neither... nor)Verb agrees with the nearest subject ("students" -> plural).Neither teacher nor students were... (Correct)
One of the + Plural NounThe main subject is "One", which is singular.One of the... factors... is...
The number ofRepresents a single specific statistic (Singular).The number of applicants has...
Each / EveryAlways singular.Each of the proposals... was...

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?

options.text: One of the books that I borrowed from the library were missing.
options.label: A

options.text: Scarcely had the train left the station when it suddenly stopped.
options.label: B

options.text: Each of the players have performed exceptionally well in the tournament.
options.label: C

options.text: The list of recommended articles are attached to the report.
options.label: D

explanation:
The Inversion Rule (Scarcely/Hardly):
When a sentence starts with a negative adverb like Hardly, Scarcely, or Barely, the sentence structure must invert: Adverb + Helping Verb + Subject.
Additionally, these words must pair with the conjunction when.
Formula: Scarcely + Had + Subject + V3 + When.
Example: Scarcely had the train left... when it stopped.
Elimination:
A) "One" takes singular "was".
C) "Each" takes singular "has".
D) "The list" takes singular "is".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The sudden announcement of the policy [ created a panic among the public ].
explanation:
The Uncountable Noun Rule:
"Panic" is an abstract, uncountable emotion. Uncountable nouns never take the indefinite articles 'A' or 'An'.
Wrong: He gave me a panic.
Right: He created panic.
Furthermore, "among the public" is the correct prepositional phrase for a large, scattered group.

question: Select the correct spelling of the word meaning "Unwilling to change one's views."
explanation:
Intransigent (In-tran-si-gent) means refusing to compromise or change one's opinions.
Memory Trick: An intransigent person will NOT TRANSfer to your side of the argument.

question: Select the correctly spelled word:
explanation:
Pusillanimous (Pu-sil-lan-i-mous) means showing a lack of courage; cowardly.
Rule of thumb for this word: One 's', Double 'l' (ll).

question:
Which of the following determiners in the sentences are correctly matched with their type?
1- Those students performed well in the examination. - Demonstrative Determiner
2- She made several mistakes in the report. - Distributive Determiner
3- Our college organizes science exhibitions every year. - Possessive Determiner
4- Each participant was given a participation certificate. - Distributive Determiner
explanation:
Determiner Classification:
WordTypeLogic
ThoseDemonstrativePoints to specific things (This, That, These, Those).
SeveralQuantifierShows an undefined amount (Many, Much, Some, Several).
It is not distributive.
OurPossessiveShows ownership (My, Your, His, Our, Their).
EachDistributiveRefers to members of a group individually (Each, Every, Either).
Since sentence 2 is incorrectly matched, the correct grouping is 1, 3, and 4.

question: In which sentence is the determiner wrongly used?

options.text: Each student was given a separate worksheet for the experiment.
options.label: A

options.text: Several researchers presented their findings at the conference.
options.label: B

options.text: Much people attended the seminar on environmental awareness.
options.label: C

options.text: Every participant signed the attendance sheet before leaving.
options.label: D

explanation:
Countable vs. Uncountable Matrix:
Much is used for Uncountable Nouns (Quantity: Much water, Much time).
Many is used for Countable Nouns (Numbers: Many boys, Many cars).
"People" is a plural, countable noun. Therefore, "Much people" is a grammatical mismatch. It must be "Many people."

question:
Match the sentence with the correct form of the verb:
Column - I (Sentence) -- Column-II (Form of Verb)
1. The scientist conducted the experiment carefully. -- i. Linking Verb
2. The child slept peacefully throughout the night. -- ii. Intransitive Verb
3. The sky became cloudy in the evening. -- iii. Auxiliary Verb
4. The students have completed the assignment. -- iv. Transitive Verb
explanation:
Verb Anatomy Test:
Sentence verbClassificationLogic
1- conducted(iv) TransitiveAction transfers to an Object. (Conducted what? The experiment).
2- slept(ii) IntransitiveAction stays with the subject. No object is needed.
3- became(i) Linking VerbConnects subject (sky) to an adjective (cloudy) without physical action.
4- have(iii) AuxiliaryA helping verb used to build the Present Perfect tense with "completed".

question:
Which form of verb is used in the sentence below?
After hours of experimentation, the reaction finally proceeded smoothly.
explanation:
Transitive vs. Intransitive Verbs:
Transitive Verbs demand a direct object. (e.g., He kicked the ball).
Intransitive Verbs do NOT take an object. (e.g., The sun rises).
In this sentence, "proceeded" is complete on its own. It does not transfer action to an object. "Smoothly" is just an adverb answering how it proceeded. Therefore, it is Intransitive.

question: As the evening progressed, the weather _____ colder.
explanation:
Tense Parallelism & Inchoative Verbs:
The sentence begins in the Simple Past tense ("As the evening progressed"). To maintain grammatical timeline parallelism, the second clause must also be in the past tense.
Present: The weather becomes colder.
Past: The weather became colder.
Fact Check: The raw input provided "become" as the correct answer. This is grammatically incorrect. "Became" is the only correct choice here.

question: Which of the following sentences contains an inchoative verb?

options.text: He writes poetry in the evening.
options.label: A

options.text: She knew the answer to the question.
options.label: B

options.text: They built a new bridge across the river.
options.label: C

options.text: The sky darkened before the storm arrived.
options.label: D

explanation:
Advanced Verb Types (Inchoative):
An Inchoative Verb is a specific type of verb that expresses a change of state, a beginning, or a becoming.
Examples: Darken (become dark), Age (become older), Ripen (become ripe), Melt (change from solid to liquid).
In Option D, "darkened" perfectly describes the sky transitioning from one state (light) to another (dark).

question:
The senator's apology was widely viewed as "too little, too late" after months of public outrage.
The idiom "too little, too late" most precisely conveys that the apology:

options.text: Failed to address the full extent of the controversy
options.label: B

options.text: Was inadequate in both substance and timing to be effective
options.label: C

options.text: Was overshadowed by more pressing political developments
options.label: D

explanation:
"Too little, too late" is a literal idiom. It means that an action or remedy is insufficient in its helpfulness (too little) and has been delayed beyond the point where it could have made a difference (too late).
Therefore, it is inadequate in both substance and timing.

question: Choose the sentence in which the correct homophone has been used.

options.text: The principal asked the students to bare the consequences of their actions.
options.label: A

options.text: She decided to compliment the dress with a matching scarf.
options.label: B

options.text: The hikers were advised to pause the trail before nightfall.
options.label: C

options.text: He could not cite a single example to support his claim.
options.label: D

explanation:
Homophones (Sound Alike, Different Meaning): Cite means to quote or refer to evidence (Correctly used here). Site means a location. Sight means vision.
Why others are incorrect:
Option A: Should be bear (to endure). Bare means naked.
Option B: Should be complement (to complete or go well with). Compliment means praise.
Option C: Should be pace (to walk at a steady speed). Pause means to stop temporarily.

question:
In which sentence is the word "bank" used as a homonym when compared to its use in the sentence below?
She deposited the cheque at the bank.

options.text: The pilot had to bank the aircraft sharply during the landing.
options.label: A

options.text: The children played on the bank of the river after school.
options.label: B

options.text: The bank approved the loan after a detailed review.
options.label: C

options.text: He works at a multinational bank in the city.
options.label: D

explanation:
Homonyms (Same Spelling/Sound, Different Meaning): The original sentence uses "bank" as a financial institution. To find its homonym, we must look for the exact same word acting as a noun but carrying a completely different meaning.
Option B uses "bank" to mean the side of a river. This is the perfect homonym.
Options C and D use "bank" in the same financial sense.
Option A uses "bank" as a verb (to tilt), which is a different part of speech.

question:
Identify the type of clause in the sentence below:
What the committee decided surprised everyone present.
The clause "What the committee decided" is a:

options.text: Noun clause functioning as the subject
options.label: A

options.text: Independent clause with an implied subject
options.label: D

explanation:
A Noun Clause acts exactly like a noun. It can be the subject or the object of a sentence.
Memory Trick: Replace the entire clause with the word "It". If the sentence still makes grammatical sense, it is a Noun Clause.
Test: [It] surprised everyone present. (Makes perfect sense).
It answers the question: What surprised everyone? The answer is the entire idea ("What the committee decided"). Therefore, it functions as the subject.

question:
The committee's proposal, though ambitious, was dismissed as "a bridge too far" by senior officials.
In this context, "a bridge too far" suggests that the proposal was:

options.text: Poorly structured and lacking practical detail
options.label: A

options.text: Excessively ambitious beyond what was feasible or acceptable
options.label: C

options.text: Intentionally provocative to test institutional boundaries
options.label: D

explanation:
Idiom "A bridge too far" refers to an act of overreaching. It describes an action, plan, or proposal that goes beyond reasonable limits and becomes excessively ambitious, impractical, or unacceptable.
Origin:* This idiom comes from a military context where trying to capture one final bridge leads to overextending forces and ultimate failure.

question:
Choose the option that correctly punctuates the sentence:
The proposal which was submitted last week however requires further revision

options.text: The proposal, which was submitted last week however, requires further revision.
options.label: A

options.text: The proposal which was submitted last week, however, requires further revision.
options.label: B

options.text: The proposal, which was submitted last week, however requires further revision.
options.label: C

options.text: The proposal, which was submitted last week, however, requires further revision.
options.label: D

explanation:
The "Extra Information" Comma Rule:
When a clause provides extra, non-essential information (a non-restrictive clause), it must be enclosed in commas.
Clause: ", which was submitted last week,"
Additionally, when transitional words like however, therefore, or moreover interrupt a sentence, they must also be hugged by commas.
Transition: ", however,"
Option D correctly isolates both the extra information and the transition word.

question:
The professor was admired for his equanimous response to harsh criticism.
Which word is the most precise antonym of equanimous?
explanation:
Equanimous means calm, composed, and even-tempered, especially in difficult situations.
WordMeaningRelationship

IndifferentLacking interest or concern.Incorrect
ImpulsiveActing without thinking.Incorrect
BelligerentAggressive or hostile.Incorrect

question: Her argument was praised for being cogent and logically compelling. Which option is the best antonym of cogent?
explanation:
Cogent means clear, logical, and thoroughly convincing.
The best antonym is Specious, which describes an argument that appears logical or convincing on the surface but is actually false or misleading.
Tentative = uncertain or not final.
Ambiguous = having multiple meanings.
Superficial = lacking depth.

question:
The editor criticized the article for its prolix treatment of an otherwise simple topic.
Which word is the most appropriate synonym of prolix in this context?
explanation:
Prolix means using far too many words; excessively long-winded.
Verbose directly matches this meaning (wordy, overly lengthy in expression).
Discursive = digressing from the main point.
Redundant = repetitive or unnecessary duplication.
Diffuse = spread out or lacking focus.

question:
The scholar was known for his perspicacious analysis of complex philosophical texts.
Which option is the closest synonym of perspicacious as used here?
explanation:
Perspicacious means having keen insight, sharp understanding, or the ability to notice and interpret things quickly and accurately.
Astute is the closest synonym, meaning sharp, perceptive, and mentally sharp.
Methodical = orderly, systematic.
Meticulous = very careful and detail-oriented.
Circumspect = cautious and careful in judgment.

question: The committee will announce the results tomorrow.

options.text: The results will be announced by the committee tomorrow.
options.label: A

options.text: The results are announced by the committee tomorrow.
options.label: B

options.text: The results will announce by the committee tomorrow.
options.label: C

options.text: The committee will be announced the results tomorrow.
options.label: D

explanation:
The Voice Transformation Rule:
To convert Future Simple from Active to Passive, use Will + BE + V3.
VoiceStructureExample
ActiveSubject + Will/Shall + V1 + ObjectThe committee will announce the results.
PassiveObject + Will/Shall + BE + V3 + by SubjectThe results will be announced by the committee.
Elimination: Option B uses Present tense ("are"). Option C uses Active structure ("will announce"). Option D makes the committee the receiver of the action.

question: She is proficient ______ French and German.
explanation:
Fixed Prepositions:
The adjective proficient (meaning skilled or competent) generally takes the preposition in when referring to a language or a broad subject area.
Memory Trick: Think of being immersed IN a language.
Example: She is proficient in English. He is proficient in mathematics.

question:
The following sentence has an error. Identify the part that contains the error.
The students (A) has submitted (B) their assignments (C) before the deadline (D).
explanation:
The Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:
The verb must agree with its subject in number
Singular Subject = Singular Verb (has, is, was, plays)
Plural Subject = Plural Verb (have, are, were, play)
Here, "The students" is a plural subject. Therefore, the singular verb "has" is incorrect. It must be replaced with the plural verb "have".

question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:
1- She practiced every day to improve her skills.
2- As a result, she won the competition.
3- She wanted to become a professional dancer.
4- Her dedication impressed her teachers.
explanation:
Chronology & Cause-Effect Link:
Always look for the "Opener" (Independent idea) and "Mandatory Pairs" (Handcuffs).
1. Opener: Statement 3 introduces her goal/intent (becoming a dancer).
2. Action: Statement 1 is the action taken to achieve that goal (practiced daily).
3. Effect: Statement 4 is the direct effect of her action (impressed teachers).
4. Result: Statement 2 contains the connector "As a result", making it the perfect concluding sentence.
Logical flow: Goal (3) → Effort (1) → Effect (4) → Final Result (2).

question:
Choose the option that correctly converts the following sentence into indirect speech:
The Professor said, "I will review your thesis tomorrow."

options.text: The professor said that he would review your thesis tomorrow.
options.label: A

options.text: The professor said that he will review your thesis the next day.
options.label: B

options.text: The professor said that he would review my thesis the next day.
options.label: C

options.text: The professor said that I would review your thesis the next day.
options.label: D

explanation:
The 3 Pillars of Narration Transformation:
When the Reporting Verb ("said") is in the past, you must backshift the tense and update the GPS (Time/Place) words.
Change typeDirect speechIndirect speech
Pronoun (SON)"I" (1st Person)"He" (Matches Subject: Professor)
Tense Backshiftwill reviewwould review
GPS / Timetomorrowthe next day
Elimination: Option A failed to change "tomorrow". Option B failed to change "will". Option D messed up the pronouns completely.

question: Choose the option that best expresses a logical deduction about a past event.

options.text: She may finish the experiment before the deadline.
options.label: A

options.text: He should have informed the committee earlier.
options.label: B

options.text: They must have overlooked the crucial data.
options.label: C

options.text: You can submit the application online.
options.label: D

explanation:
Past Modals (The Deduction vs. Regret Rule):
To express an action that happened in the past, we use Modal + Have + V3.
Modal structureMeaningExample
Must have + V3Logical Deduction (99% sure it happened)The streets are wet; it must have rained.
Should have + V3Regret / Unfulfilled DutyI failed; I should have studied.
Addressing your confusion: Option B ("should have") expresses a regret or a mistake that wasn't fixed. Option C ("must have") is a logical conclusion/deduction based on evidence. Since the question specifically asks for a "logical deduction", C is the correct answer.

question: Choose the sentence in which the use of articles is grammatically and contextually correct.

options.text: She is a expert in medieval literature.
options.label: A

options.text: The committee reached an unanimous decision.
options.label: B

options.text: An honest administrator is essential for effective governance.
options.label: C

options.text: He goes to the bed at 10 PM daily.
options.label: D

explanation:
The Article Sound Rule & Primary Purpose Rule:
Articles are based on sound, not spelling.
Option A is wrong: "Expert" starts with an 'E' sound (Vowel). It must be "an expert".
Option B is wrong: "Unanimous" starts with a 'Yoo' sound (Consonant). It must be "a unanimous decision".
Option D is wrong: When visiting a bed for its primary purpose (sleeping), the "Zero Article" rule applies. It should be "goes to bed"[cite: 1].
Option C is correct: "Honest" has a silent 'H' (On-est = Vowel sound), so it correctly takes "An". Abstract nouns like "governance" take zero article.

question: Identify the sentence with a clear and unambiguous pronoun reference.

options.text: When Sara met Lina, she was already upset.
options.label: A

options.text: The manager told the clerk that he needed to lock the door.
options.label: B

options.text: Rahul told Amit that he had won the scholarship.
options.label: C

options.text: After the report was revised, it was criticized by the editor.
options.label: D

explanation:
Pronoun Ambiguity Rule:
A pronoun must clearly refer to one specific noun (its antecedent). If there are two nouns of the same gender/type in a sentence, using "he" or "she" creates a confusing, ambiguous sentence.
Option A: Does "she" refer to Sara or Lina? (Ambiguous)
Option B: Does "he" refer to the manager or the clerk? (Ambiguous)
Option C: Does "he" refer to Rahul or Amit? (Ambiguous)
Option D: "It" clearly refers to the only neuter noun in the sentence, "the report". (Unambiguous)

question: Choose the sentence in which the pronoun usage is grammatically correct.

options.text: Each of the participants must submit their assignment by Friday.
options.label: A

options.text: Neither of the proposals achieved their intended objective.
options.label: B

options.text: Every applicant should bring his or her identification for verification.
options.label: C

options.text: The committee reached their decision after prolonged deliberation.
options.label: D

explanation:
Indefinite Pronouns & Singular Identity:
Words like Each, Every, Either, and Neither treat individuals one by one. They are always singular. Because they take a singular verb, they must also take a singular possessive pronoun.
Wrong: Each of the boys brought their bag. (Plural pronoun)
Right: Each of the boys brought his bag. (Singular pronoun)
Elimination: Options A and B incorrectly use "their". Option D uses "their" for "committee", but a collective noun acting as a single unit should take "its" (reached its decision). Option C correctly pairs "Every" with the singular formal pronoun "his or her".
